inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E = midpoint of the raised 4-Nov-2026 guidance ($16.37-16.43bn); 9M-2026 actual $12,679m + Q4 guide $3.69-3.75bn. FY2025 actual was $14,733m. Growth path compounds from FY2026E, so Y1 = FY2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30-Sep-2026: 113.122m common + 5.523m Class B outstanding (10-Q cover/balance sheet) + 2.413m dilutive stock awards (Q3-2026 EPS note). Convertible Notes settled in cash Feb-2026 so no longer dilutive. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count; buybacks ($1.73bn 9M-2026, $1.93bn FY2025) are the cash mechanism keeping the count flat and are not separately credited.
inputs.cash_note: Unrestricted cash $5,040m + short-term investments $527m at 30-Sep-2026. Restricted cash ($1,543m, traveler deposits) EXCLUDED. Unrestricted cash is largely merchant float offset by $12.6bn deferred merchant bookings; treated as a financial asset at face while the float growth is credited only partially via wc_capture_pct and float interest income is excluded from the projected flows (Adjusted EBITDA is pre-interest) -- so the cash is counted exactly once.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income $255m is left in last_fcf because unrestricted net cash ($107m) is immaterial (<<1x FCF base) -- stripping it would un-count a float the bridge barely credits. The forward build starts from Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes interest income and expense, so projected flows carry neither.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back $398m (Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation uses the same figure); plus $65m cash withholding taxes on net-share settlement (9M-2026 statement of stockholders' equity, 'Withholding taxes for stock options', annualised ~$65m; FY2025 equity statement showed only $28m). No combined company figure is published, so the two lines are summed. 9M-2026 SBC amortisation $337m -> ~$450m FY2026E (2.7% of revenue).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchases of treasury stock $1,930m; 9M-2026 $1,727m. $5.1bn remained authorised at 30-Sep-2026 (2023 + May-2026 programs). Repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:01Z regular close (two sessions after the 4-Nov Q3 print; the -8.5% after-hours reaction is already in the close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Rf 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.4 (travel cyclical) -> cost of equity ~11.3%; cost of debt 5.4-5.5% on the 2035/2036 notes, ~4.3% after tax; market cap ~$31bn vs $5.5bn debt -> 85/15 -> WACC ~10.2%, rounded to 10.0%. Same WACC in all scenarios; scenario risk is carried in the paths and weights, not in a per-scenario rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating lease cost (ROU assets $278m, liabilities $226m LT + current) is inside Adjusted EBITDA as an operating expense (ASC 842 operating leases), so it is already charged in the flows; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. Immaterial either way (<2% of EBITDA).
inputs.nci_treatment: trivago non-controlling interest (book $1,264m) is deducted in the equity bridge at an approximate market value of $200m rather than book -- trivago's listed market value is a fraction of its carrying amount and its segment EBITDA (~$19m/quarter) does not support book. Flows are consolidated (100% of trivago), so the NCI is charged once, in the bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon (margins still ramping at year 5), per dcf-methods SKILL.md routing row 'operating company: consumer internet, marketplaces'. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). EBITDA margin paths are on an UNDERLYING basis: company Adjusted EBITDA margin (FY2025 23.8%, FY2026E ~25.7% per guidance) less ~0.8pp for the restructuring and legal-reserve/occupancy-tax charges that Adjusted EBITDA excludes but which have recurred every year (FY2024 $190m, FY2025 $285m, 9M-2026 $59m net). Working capital: the merchant model's deferred-merchant-bookings float grew $1,858m in FY2025 (WC inflow $1,173m = 113% of the revenue increase; 3-yr average ~60%); only 30% capture is credited in base because the float reverses violently in a downturn (FY2020 FCF -$4.6bn). Float interest income (~$255m/yr) is excluded from projected flows; unrestricted cash is in the bridge at face. Cash tax rate ramps from ~16% (FY2025 cash taxes $218m on $1,591m pre-tax = 13.7%; GAAP ETR 18.2%) to 22% by year 5 -- the IRS transfer-pricing dispute signals the current low cash rate is not a safe perpetuity. Terminal cap 15x (cyclical) in base/bull, 12x in bear. Price is a regular close; not after-hours.

equity_bridge.item: trivago non-controlling interest at approximate market value
equity_bridge.note: Book NCI $1,264m at 30-Sep-2026 (10-Q balance sheet); deducted at ~40% of an estimated ~$500m trivago market value, not at book. See inputs.nci_treatment.

Q3-2026 10-Q: IRS proposes ~$1.0-1.2bn additional federal tax for 2011-2018 plus interest; Expedia disputes. ~30% of the midpoint as an expected cash outcome. Bear narrative assumes a worse outcome; bull assumes substantially prevailing.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Blend of revenue 3-yr CAGR (FY2022-25, 8.1%) and FY2019-25 CAGR (3.4%), anchored to FY2026 guidance (+11%) decelerating as Q4-2026 bookings guide (+3-5%) and B2B comps bite; equity CAGR is negative and meaningless for a company retiring ~8% of its shares a year and is NOT used.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-12%/yr) diverges >30% from revenue (+8%) and EPS (+66%) CAGRs: book equity is shrinking because $1.8-2.1bn/yr of buybacks exceed retained earnings, not because the business is shrinking. Treat equity CAGR as uninformative here.
historical_growth.notes: '5yr' figures use FY2019 as the base (6 years) because FY2020-21 are COVID-distorted (FY2020 FCF -$4.6bn, FY2021 EPS negative) and a negative base makes the CAGR undefined. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2019 1,366 / FY2022 2,404 / FY2023 1,431 / FY2024 1,871 / FY2025 2,712. Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR (4.1%) slightly above reported (3.8%) because SBC fell from $374m to $398m while FCF grew -- SBC is NOT outgrowing cash flow here; it has drifted down from 3.2% to 2.7% of revenue.

base.narrative: FY2027 revenue +7% as the Q4-2026 deceleration (bookings +3-5%, election-cycle softness, Middle East/Europe disruption, tough B2B comps) carries into H1-2027, then a glide to 3% as online-travel penetration matures; B2B (+20%+) keeps the blend above B2C. Underlying EBITDA margin expands ~2pp over ten years (platform unification, cost of revenue and tech/content leverage) to 27% -- half the gap to Booking's ~35%, net of the ~0.8pp of recurring 'non-recurring' charges. SBC drifts 2.7% -> 2.3%. Cash tax normalises to 22%. 30% of the revenue increase captured as float.

bull.narrative: B2B/Partner Solutions sustains ~20% growth and reaches ~45% of revenue; agentic-AI integrations (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Alexa+) prove to be a net new distribution channel that lowers paid-search dependence; trivago and EG Advertising keep compounding high-margin ad revenue. Underlying margin reaches 31% (approaching Booking) as direct marketing falls as a share of revenue. The IRS dispute is substantially won (the bridge provision is then too harsh). Float capture 40%.

bear.narrative: AI answer-engines and Google's own travel surfaces disintermediate OTA discovery: traffic-acquisition cost rises faster than revenue, B2C bookings stall and the margin expansion of 2024-26 reverses to 23%. B2B growth slows as partners negotiate commissions down and airlines push direct-connect. A 2027 consumer slowdown keeps revenue growth at 2-3%, the float stops growing (15% capture), and the IRS/Italian tax matters settle closer to the proposed amounts, pushing the cash tax rate to 24%. Terminal multiple capped at 12x for a slow-growth cyclical.

scenario_narratives.base: Travel demand normalises after the FY2026 shocks; Expedia grows revenue 7% decelerating to 3%, led by B2B, while unified-platform cost leverage lifts underlying EBITDA margin ~2pp to 27%. Buybacks keep the share count flat against 2.3-2.7% SBC. Cash taxes normalise toward 22% and the IRS dispute costs roughly a third of the proposed amount.
scenario_narratives.bull: B2B compounds at ~20% to nearly half of revenue, AI-agent distribution is a net share gainer rather than a threat, ad revenue scales, and margins converge toward Booking's at 31%. Growth 9% fading to 4%, float capture 40%, terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI disintermediation and supplier direct-connect raise acquisition costs and stall B2C; growth 2-3%, margin reverts to 23%, float stops contributing, tax disputes settle adversely. Capped at a 12x terminal multiple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the two high-severity risks in the Analysis -- agentic-AI disintermediation of OTA discovery and the $1.0-1.2bn IRS transfer-pricing claim -- are both live and both outside management's control, and Q4-2026 guidance shows how quickly demand can decelerate. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once (B2B momentum sustained, AI as a net-positive channel, margin convergence toward Booking). Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Expedia is valued as a mature, cash-generative marketplace on fully SBC-expensed owner FCF with a flat share count. The merchant-model float is treated conservatively: cash is counted once at face, float growth is only partially credited and float interest is excluded from projected flows. Adjusted EBITDA is haircut for the restructuring and legal charges that recur every year. The IRS dispute and the trivago minority are explicit bridge deductions so a reader can remove them. Scenario risk (AI disintermediation, cyclicality, tax) is carried in the paths and a 25% bear weight, not stacked into WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Agentic AI / Google travel surfaces redirect discovery away from OTAs, raising traffic-acquisition cost -- the bear margin path
IRS transfer-pricing claim ($1.0-1.2bn proposed plus interest) resolves above the $350m provision; Italian withholding-tax matters
Travel cyclicality: a demand downturn reverses the deferred-merchant-bookings float (FY2020 FCF was -$4.6bn)
B2B partner-commission costs grow faster than B2B revenue, so segment mix shift adds less margin than assumed
Terminal value is ~half of EV; a 1pp move in WACC moves the base value materially -- see sensitivity grid
Barry Diller's Class B voting control and recent leadership turnover (governance)
